text:
Kai: uploaded cross-region A100/H100 prefill+decode bench for Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B (4bit/8bit). s3://redwood-bench/2067890123/index.html TL;DR: H100 ~1.9x tokens/sec on decode for 13B, but A100 is still cheaper $/1M tokens in eu-west-1 for high-batch workloads.
Maria: nice — can you paste the short numbers? trying to size Dedicated pools.
Kai: sure, quick table (prefill p50 / decode p95 / tokens/sec / $/1M tokens)
```
Region  GPU  Model        Quant  Prefill_p50  Decode_p95  tok/s  $/1M
us-west-2 A100 Llama2-13B 4-bit   180ms       340ms      420   $8.7
us-west-2 H100 Llama2-13B 4-bit   120ms       190ms      800   $15.5
eu-west-1 A100 Llama2-13B 8-bit   200ms       420ms      360   $7.9
eu-west-1 H100 Llama2-13B 8-bit   140ms       230ms      690   $14.8
us-west-2 A100 Mistral-7B 4-bit   95ms        130ms      1250  $6.1
us-west-2 H100 Mistral-7B 4-bit   70ms        80ms       2200  $10.9
```
Kai: notes — numbers are median of 5 runs, 2k request sample, synthetic chat-like prompts (prefill ~128 tokens, decode 32 tokens). token/sec measured per-GPU sustained.
Oliver: what about kernel flavors? flash vs cutlass vs tensorkernel fallthrough? any stability/ooms?
Kai: did three kernel configs: default runtime pick, force-flash-attn, force-cutlass. Findings: H100+flash gave best latency for decode tails, but on some dense prompt shapes flash had +OOMs at 4-bit on Llama2-13B -> we ended up with fallbacks to cutlass for p95 stability. A100 prefers cutlass for 4-bit quant workloads.
Sophie: quant tradeoffs? any visible quality regressions at 4-bit for 13B?
Kai: did 100 eval prompts (comp-similarity & exact-match). 4-bit Llama2-13B had tiny BLEU-ish drop (~0.6 points) vs 8-bit, generally within noise for/chat apps. Mistral-7B more robust to 4-bit in our tests.
Maria: for Dedicated sizing — if I want 99th percentile latency <300ms for decode for Llama2-13B in eu-west-1, is H100 necessary?
Kai: short answer: yes for single-GPU requests at low-batch. H100 p95 decode ~230ms (8-bit) in eu-west-1 so margin exists. A100 would need batching (batch size >=4) to hit p95<300ms but throughput cost goes up.
Maria: cost calc? assume 1M requests, avg 160 tokens per request?
Kai: rough: use the $/1M tokens above — convert tokens/request*1M/1e6. For 160 tokens/request, tokens = 160M, so cost = (160 * $/1M) e.g. H100 eu-west-1 8-bit: 160*$14.8 = $2368, A100 eu-west-1 8-bit: 160*$7.9 = $1264. But H100 latency margin might reduce need for multi-GPU or queueing.
bench-bot: bench run 2067890123 completed in 58m 42s. Artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/2067890123/{raw,plots,configs}.
Oliver: can you add kernel policy suggestion to the console rollout? fallback: flash->cutlass->runtime. Also add a note to avoid forcing flash on 4-bit 13B in eu-west-1.
Kai: yep will file a PR to rollout config. quick snippet for the policy to paste into console rollout:
```
kernel_policy:
  preferred: [flash-attn, cutlass, runtime]
  fallbacks:
    flash-attn: [cutlass, runtime]
    cutlass: [runtime]
```
Sophie: thanks — any anomalies?
Kai: one weirdness: on us-west-2 A100 Llama2-13B 4-bit had higher prefill variance when host CPU was over 70% — likely packing/PCIe copy contention in our test cluster. Added note to infra.
Maria: perfect. can you tag the Dedicated sizing doc and we’ll mark this as reference for bookings? :thumbsup:
Kai: done — tagged rfc/dedicated-sizing with link to artifact.
Sophie: :eyes: will run a smaller real-traffic check later today.
Maria: great work, thanks team.
